title: A uniform law can grow flat space but not the knot's contradiction
subject: Which laws of lines and co-lines with one kind of point close into spheres, and whether the knot's count forces a contradiction on them
conclusion: A law of lines and co-lines builds its own closed surface; with one kind of point it closes into a sphere only as an antiprism or a snub polyhedron of at most 60 points. With uniform signs the count never forces the knot's lines on any uniform law, and Kasteleyn signs make the knot fail only on those small spheres or antiprism chains solvable in O(log n) queries, so a deep contradiction needs a second kind of point.
